title: South Africa commercial entry playbook
content:
Summary / purpose:
This playbook is a pragmatic, sales-and-ops focused launch brief for Redwood Inference’s commercial rollout in South Africa (ZA). It covers target segments, positioning and messaging, competitive signals, partner and pilot tactics, sales enablement artifacts, compliance notes (POPIA & data residency), pricing guidance, and a recommended 90-day go-to-market timeline. Purpose is to align GTM, partnerships, product, and legal on a low-friction market entry that emphasizes developer velocity, predictable inference economics, and private deployment options for regulated customers.

Key objectives (90-day):
- Sign 3 pilot customers (1 fintech, 1 contact center, 1 enterprise SaaS) on dedicated or private deployments.
- Validate latency/cost value prop vs public endpoints with a 20% unit-cost improvement target for typical contact-center workloads.
- Establish 2 channel partnerships (local cloud reseller or SI + managed service partner).
- Deliver sales enablement pack and run two customer-facing technical workshops in JHB/CPT.

Why South Africa now (rationale):
- Growing enterprise interest in LLM features (summarization, routing, virtual agents) and a preference for provider options that offer data residency and private deployments.
- Strong local partner ecosystem (SIs, cloud resellers) that can bundle inference into contact-center and fintech solutions.
- Regulatory environment (POPIA) increases demand for private deployments and auditability — a fit for Redwood Private and Dedicated.

Target segments and buyer personas:
1) Financial services (retail banks, payments fintechs): CIO/Head of Engineering, Security/Compliance, Head of Digital Channels. Must-haves: audit trails, KMS integrations, predictable costs.
2) Contact centers / BPOs: Head of CX / CTO. Must-haves: real-time low-latency inference, high throughput, cost controls for high-volume transcripts.
3) Enterprise SaaS (HR, legal automation): Product lead / Platform engineer. Must-haves: integration support, model versioning, rollout controls.
4) Public sector (selected agencies): Procurement lead / IT director — later stage; requires procurement/legal prep.

Positioning and core messaging (value props):
- For engineering teams building production LLM features: "Ship predictable, cost-efficient LLM inference with full deployment options — hosted, reserved, or private — so you control latency, cost, and compliance."
- Differentiators to emphasize: unified runtime across environments, per-token cost transparency, SLA-backed dedicated capacity, and KMS/HSM integrations for private deployments.
- Local messaging hooks: "Available in-region options and partner-managed private deployments to meet POPIA & audit requirements."

Competitive landscape (local + global):
- Major cloud vendors (AWS/GCP/Azure): strong presence; customers may try managed endpoints. Differentiator: Redwood’s inference economics, specialized serving runtime, and easy private control plane.
- Global LLM APIs (OpenAI, Anthropic, other hosted vendors): easier to start but weaker for data residency/private installs and unit-cost predictability at scale.
- Local SIs & consultancies (implementation partners): potential partners rather than direct competitors; they can resell or co-sell.
- Regional niche startups (conversational agents): aggressive on vertical features but limited on scale & deployment options.

Top competitive talking points (battlecard snippets):
- If customer says "We can just use public endpoints": respond with latency and cost examples on 1M monthly messages + POPIA risks for sensitive data; present Redwood Dedicated & Private.
- If customer says "We already have an on-prem solution": ask about ongoing ops cost, model upgrades, and dev velocity; highlight Redwood’s managed private control plane and rollout tools.
- Price objection: show per-token TCO and batching/cache benefits plus predictable reserved pricing. Offer pilot credits on first 30 days to demonstrate delta.

Regional compliance & security notes:
- Primary regulation: POPIA — data residency and personal data processing accountability. For customers with strict residency needs push Redwood Private (VPC/on-prem) or Dedicated pools with regionally isolated storage.
- KMS/HSM: call out our supported integrations and include an internal link to product docs for KMS setup.
- Procurement: anticipate SOW + security questionnaire for enterprise; prepare a standard redlines matrix and an accelerated review checklist for pilots.

Sales enablement assets (to produce quickly):
- SA battlecard (1-pager) with objections and win themes — due week 1.
- Technical one-pager: deployment options + latency/cost examples + network/KMS checklist.
- Pilot offer template and SOW addendum for private/Dedicated pilots.
- 45-min technical workshop slide deck and lab guide (sample prompts, perf tests).
- One internal FAQ for SRE/product on expected infra support and SLOs.

Suggested announcement and outreach copy (internal-first draft):
- Email subject lines: "Redwood Inference — Commercial availability in South Africa (pilot program)"; "Bring LLM inference on-prem or in-region with Redwood — Cape Town & Joburg workshops"
- Short press/partner pitch: "Redwood Inference launches commercial entry into South Africa with in-region deployment options and partner-managed private installs to help enterprises adopt LLM features while meeting POPIA and cost demands."
- Developer community blurb: "Join our Cape Town workshop — hands-on with Redwood Dedicated and Private deployments, model rollouts, and cost-optimization best practices."

Launch channels & tactics:
- Direct outbound to existing Redwood leads with ZA interest (email + SDR calls) — week 1–4.
- Partner pilots: engage 3 SIs for co-selling and joint demos — week 1–8.
- Events: host 2 hybrid technical workshops (JHB & CPT) and one webinar targeted at fintech/contact-center tech leads — week 6–10.
- Content: publish one partner case short (pilot results), two blog posts (technical + business), and localized PR outreach to tech press — week 6–12.

Pricing & commercial offers (guidance):
- Pilot offer: free trial credits + discounted reserved capacity for 3 months to validate throughput and latencies.
- GTM list-price guidance: follow existing regional pricing bands, but offer flexible commit terms for Dedicated pools and bespoke pricing for private engagement.
- Channel margins: standard partner discount tier for resellers (TBD with Partnerships team).

Operational readiness checklist (pre-launch):
- Confirm region support for Dedicated pools (infra engineering sign-off).
- Legal: finalize POPIA-specific addendum and standard SOW templates.
- Billing: enable ZA tax handling and invoicing workflow for local contracts.
- Support: establish a local on-call rotation for pilot period and predefine escalation paths.

Risks & mitigations:
- Low initial pipeline: mitigate by fast partner onboarding and targeted joint webinars.
- Procurement lead times: offer shorter pilot SOW + templated security responses to reduce procurement friction.
- Technical integration surprises: require an early discovery call and offer a paid discovery if integration is complex.

Metrics to track (first 90 days):
- Number of qualified pilots (target 3).
- Time from initial contact to pilot launch (target < 30 days).
- Pilot-to-paid conversion rate.
- Average per-token unit cost delta vs public endpoints for pilot workloads.

90-day timeline (high level):
- Week 0–2: internal enablement, partner shortlist, finalize pilot SOW & legal addendum.
- Week 2–6: outbound + partner outreach, select pilot customers, run initial technical workshops.
- Week 6–12: execute pilots, publish early pilot results (anonymized), host regional workshops/webinar, begin commercial negotiations.

Next steps (action owners):
- Partnerships: finalize partner list and intro decks (owner: Diego Alvarez) — due 2026-03-07.
- Product/Infra: confirm Dedicated regional availability and KMS playbook (owner: Priya Malhotra) — due 2026-03-05.
- Legal: draft POPIA addendum and pilot SOW template (owner: Ethan Ross) — due 2026-03-04.
- Sales: prepare battlecard + pilot price templates (owner: Anele Dlamini) — due 2026-03-06.

Appendix / quick assets (to attach in final pack):
- One-pager technical checklist (network, keys, latency targets).
- Pilot SOW template.
- Email drip sequence for pilot prospects.

Notes & open questions:
- Confirm whether we will purchase local cloud egress capacity or rely solely on partner-managed infra for Dedicated pools.
- Need input from finance on local billing and tax setup for ZA contracts.
- Do we want Afrikaans localization for any customer-facing docs or purely English initially? Recommendation: English first; add ZA-local language only for large enterprise customers if requested.

Owner & contact: Thandiwe Nkosi (thandiwe@redwood.ai) — ping in #gtm-africa channel for immediate coordination.

Document history: created 2025-11-02; major revision 2026-02-28 to update pilot offer and timeline after product infra review.
